rv.q: This is a potent story, told with imagination and flair.

If the philosophical and religious discussions erode some of the pace from the drama, particularly in the final 30 minutes or so, the play demands that its audience confront what are today called culture wars.
But if you’re going to make a short story a two-and-a-half-hour play, it’s going to need more subtext, less exposition.

cn.t: This Australian adaptation returns to Singer's original story with theatrical richness and modern resonance, though critics are mixed on its execution, praising its roots in Yiddish theatre tradition while questioning its overall impact.
